title: CAMTS board members join pediatric transport leaders at AAP Section on Transport Medicine Program
summary: Dr. Robert Holcomb and Tammy Rush represent CAMTS as the Section on Transport Medicine convenes on safety, quality and neonatal-pediatric care
body_markdown:
The Commission on Accreditation of Medical Transport Systems (CAMTS) participated in the American Academy of Pediatrics (AAP) Section on Transport Medicine (SOTM) Program on Sunday, October 4, 2026.


CAMTS board members Dr. Robert Holcomb and Ms. Tammy Rush, along with CAMTS executive director Jan Eichel, joined neonatal and pediatric transport clinicians, researchers and program leaders for a full day of education, research and recognition.


Dr. Holcomb represents the AAP on the CAMTS Board of Directors, and Rush represents the National Association of Neonatal Nurses (NANN). CAMTS also co-sponsored the program’s evening Reception and Awards Ceremony.


The program focused on safety, quality and clinical care in neonatal and pediatric transport, with sessions on QI metrics, lights and sirens, aviation safety and airway management.


CAMTS Pghoto


The afternoon included an Honorary Lecture by Lifetime Achievement Award winner Bruce Klein, MD, FAAP, twelve oral abstract presentations and the Don Null, MD, FAAP Research Seed Grant presentations.


The meeting also marked the release of the AAP’s[Guidelines for Air and Ground Transport of Neonatal and Pediatric Patients , 5th Edition](https://www.aap.org/Guidelines-for-Air-Ground-Transport-of-Neonatal-and-Pediatric-Patients-5th-Edition-Paperback) , the Section’s core reference for transport programs caring for infants and children. Dr. Holcomb and Rush both contributed to the new edition.


“Forums like the Section on Transport Medicine shape how programs assess safety and quality and are guided by our accreditation standards,” said Jan Eichel, executive director of CAMTS.


“We sincerely thank Dr. Holcomb and Ms. Rush for representing CAMTS’ unwavering commitment to safety and excellence in transport and for their inspiring leadership in these efforts.”


*This press release was prepared and distributed by CAMTS.*
